newsitem.title: USA: "Professionals only" commods markets dangerous - SEC.
newsitem.headline: "Professionals only" commods markets dangerous - SEC.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) opposes a proposal in a U.S. House bill to authorize professionals-only markets at commodity exchanges, said Richard Lindsey, SEC director of market regulation.

Lindsey said on Tuesday the plan "would expose futures markets to additional risk of manipulation, call into question the validity of the exchanges as price discovery mechanisms and place undue pressure on clearing mechanisms for both professional market and retail market transactions."
It also would violate the Shad-Johnson accord that gives SEC a role in approval of stock index futures, he said.

In testimony to a House Agriculture subcommittee looking at revisions to the basic U.S. law regulating the futures industry, Lindsey said the "pro" market exemption proposed in H.R. 467 was overly broad and "would result in a dangerous and unprecedented restructuring of exchange markets into a two-tiered system..."

The bill would exempt professionals-only market from federal regulation except for antifraud and antimanipulation provisions of the Commodity Exchange Act, he said. Participants would not be subject to audit trails, books and records and surveillance requirements they now face, he said.
As an alternative, Lindsey said the CFTC and the major U.S. exchanges should work on development of the "pro" market pilot program proposed by CFTC in 1995.
He also proposed exclusion from CEA of privately negotiated institutional over-the-counter transactions in securities-based swaps.

The so-called Treasury amendment should be clarified, he said, to limit CFTC jurisdiction to exchange-traded futures and options on futures and to say that options on securities, or groups or indices of securities, were exempt from CEA.
